summary.headline: Marico guides FY27 to double-digit revenue growth past INR15,000 crore and high-teens EBITDA growth, assuming macro normalises, after copra fell ~35% from peak.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of multi-year highs in India volume growth, International constant-currency growth and consolidated revenue, with double-digit profit growth despite sharp input inflation. Copra has corrected about 35% from peak and is expected to stay range-bound, while vegetable oils and crude-linked inputs are rising on Middle East tensions. Marico passed on copra benefits through price cuts of about 10% on non-price-point and small packs of Parachute, and took 6-7% price increases in VAHO. The FY27 guidance was raised to high-teens EBITDA growth, and the FY30 aspiration was set at mid-teens EBITDA growth with revenue crossing INR20,000 crore.

financial_highlights.value: Double-digit growth to cross INR15,000 crore

financial_highlights.change: Raised vs prior call (previously mid-teens, per management)
Gross margin +350-400 bps over FY26 exit; A&P up 200-250 bps
Inflated by denominator effect from revenue growth
Mid-teens growth in FY26; ~16-17% in Q4 incl. acquisitions

financial_highlights.value: INR350+ crore (Serums, Male Grooming, Skin Care); INR1,100+ crore digital-first portfolio

financial_highlights.metric: Foods + Premium Personal Care share of India business

segments.name: Parachute (India coconut oil)
segments.commentary: Delivered low single-digit volume growth after adjusting for mlage; non-price-point and small packs cut by ~10% as copra fell ~35% from peak. Management says RPI is not significantly off despite ~60% price increase taken last year.

segments.name: Value Added Hair Oils (VAHO)
segments.commentary: Volume growth in low-20s% in Q4 and ~20% for FY26, led by mid and premium segments growing close to double-digit on a two-year CAGR. Took 6-7% price increase in response to crude-derivative inflation; expects double-digit volume-led growth.

segments.name: Saffola Edible Oils
segments.commentary: Steady performance in an elevated pricing environment; guided to low-to-mid single-digit volume growth subject to a margin threshold, with pricing passed on and focus on Saffola Gold, Total and cold-pressed.

segments.name: Foods
segments.commentary: Mid-teens growth in FY26; core Saffola Foods grew double digits in Q4, while True Elements lapped a high base and SKU rationalisation. Management base case is 20-25% growth in FY27.

segments.name: Premium Personal Care / digital-first brands
segments.commentary: Beardo and Plix on accelerated growth with improving profitability; Plix estimated at mid-to-high single-digit EBITDA margin, targeting double digits soon. Aim to exit FY27 at double-digit EBITDA margin and teens by FY30.

segments.name: International business
segments.commentary: Bangladesh grew 35% in the latest quarter vs 25% for the full year, with guidance of at least double-digit growth. Vietnam, South Africa and exports are scaling; Middle East (4% of turnover) hit by March supply constraints, with alternate routes via Egypt. FY27 guided to mid-teens constant-currency growth.

guidance_outlook: FY27 India volume growth: high single-digit; International: mid-teens constant-currency growth.
FY27 consolidated: double-digit revenue growth to cross INR15,000 crore and high-teens EBITDA growth, assuming normalisation of macros; management said it is a best-case view given crude uncertainty.
FY27 gross margin expansion of about 350-400 bps over FY26 exit; operating margin expansion about 150 bps after higher A&P.

FY30 aspirations: revenue to comfortably cross INR20,000 crore, mid-teens EBITDA growth; Foods+PPC share of India business to about one-third by FY30; commodity-linked share to fall from over 70% to 50% over a decade.
Weighted average input cost increase for FY27 described as extremely marginal, with price hikes said to neutralise the impact.
capex_capacity: No specific capacity, utilisation or capex figures were discussed in the call.
Acquisitions cited: 4700BC, Cosmix (profitable, high-teens margin) and Skinetiq (mid-20s margin); integration described as positive with no hiccups, and modern trade synergies started.
Supply chain: company says it is well stocked on raw materials, packaging and finished goods, with no material disruption foreseen near term.
demand_pricing: Demand sentiment broadly stable in Q4; more than 95% of portfolio gaining or sustaining share and over 90% maintaining or improving penetration on MAT basis.
Parachute: copra corrected ~35% from peak, price cut ~10% on non-price-point packs; expects volume pickup visible from Q1 FY27.
Competition: smaller players constrained by packaging, polymer and working-capital pressures; management believes this supports share gains.
Core Saffola Foods grew double digits in Q4; Foods overall growth partly held back by True Elements base effects and SKU rationalisation.
Management flagged risks from West Asia inflation, monsoon onset and a possible strong El Nino affecting H2 FY27 consumption.

qa_highlights.question: Why was EBITDA guidance raised despite acquisition drag and sharp crude-derivative inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a firmer copra view, acquisitions (Cosmix, Skinetiq) already profitable, improved digital margins and procurement synergies; the guidance is a best-case view and stress-tested for crude.

qa_highlights.question: Why are FY27 margins below historic peaks?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak years had low commodity inflation; expansion of 150 bps operating margin is planned, with A&P increased 200-250 bps and denominator effect from revenue growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will Parachute price cuts be cross-subsidised by inflationary categories?
qa_highlights.answer: Management takes a portfolio approach, with ~10% cut on non-price-point and small packs; it sees a competitive advantage from smaller players' supply issues rather than cross-subsidising.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Plix and its profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Plix is at mid-to-high single-digit EBITDA margin, targeting double digits; D2C is ~45% of the business, and the brand is pivoting to personal care with nutraceutical launches (ACV canned drink).

qa_highlights.question: What are the top risks for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Macro and geopolitical factors, inflation hitting FMCG consumption (especially rural/bottom of pyramid), and a strong El Nino affecting H2 FY27 and Q1 FY28; internal execution is seen as on track.

risks_watch: Crude and crude-derivative inflation (VAHO, packaging) versus copra tailwind; guidance assumes normalisation and management said visibility improves after 1-2 quarters.
Middle East supply disruption and Gulf sales; MENA is 4% of turnover.
Monsoon, El Nino and West Asia-driven inflation affecting rural consumption and down-trading.
Sustainability of VAHO growth given industry-wide strong growth and possible reversal if copra prices fall.
Plix scale and growth beyond INR1,000 crore ARR; Foods growth delivery vs 20-25% base case; Bangladesh growth normalisation after 35% quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, FY27 guidance and the copra tailwind, while repeatedly caveating that guidance depends on crude and macro normalisation. Management was evasive on specific MENA April trends and on Plix margin and channel questions, answering in broad terms.
key_quotes: At a consolidated level, we aim to deliver double -digit revenue growth to cross INR15,000 crores in revenues and high -teen EBITDA growth, subject to stable macros.
I think we would be the only company who would be giving this kind of a guidance in this kind of environment of high-teen EBITDA growth.

growth.why: FY27 guided to double-digit revenue growth past INR15,000 crore and high-teens EBITDA growth (conditional on macro normalisation), with high single-digit India volume growth and mid-teens International constant-currency growth, but no specific capacity, capex or order book was discussed, so backing is vague.
